title: Personal Ops + Telegram Bot
tagline: Personal agenda with a local-LLM conversation bot

simple.tagline: My calendar and my workouts, controlled through a Telegram conversation.
simple.summary: I brought together my personal routine and my college handball team's training plan into one system. The key difference is I don't need to open anything: I talk to it on Telegram, it reminds me of what's still pending throughout the day, and when I say "wrap up the day," it closes out the summary.

problem: Centralize personal routine and university handball training planning in a single system — with proactive reminders and conversational control through Telegram, at zero LLM API cost and without sending personal data to third parties.
targetUser: Personal use (single authenticated user, server bound to localhost).
process: Implemented a single Flask server for site and REST API; no-build frontend (plain HTML/CSS/JS, Tailwind and FullCalendar via CDN); data in plain JSON — deliberately no database. The Telegram conversation bot runs on a local model (Ollama): free-form questions about the agenda, create/edit/complete/delete for tasks and events, and batch actions — always with explicit confirmation before writing. Automatic notifications with periodic summaries and an independent watchdog that alerts when the server goes down.
keyDecisions: Radical simplicity: Flask + JSON + CDN — zero build, zero infrastructure; the app starts from a .bat in Windows Startup.
Every conversation-triggered write requires a "yes/no" confirmation before saving — batch actions included, with the real item list displayed before confirming.
When information is missing (event location, actual completion date), the bot asks instead of assuming — parsing "today", "yesterday", weekdays and explicit dates.
Dual authentication: browser session for the UI, Bearer token for automation.
Anti-hallucination in code, not in the prompt: model-generated notifications are only accepted if they mention every real item title; otherwise the system falls back to deterministic text.
result: In daily use: full CRUD via web and via conversation, periodic summaries until an "end the day" command, actual-completion date separate from the deadline, date-grouped UI with a completed section, and a watchdog reporting server downtime and recovery.
learned: Local models hallucinate even under an explicit "never invent" instruction — the protection that works is validating output in code against real data, with a deterministic fallback. The simplest possible stack (no build, no database) is a feature when the goal is operating every day with zero maintenance.
